electrical_safety_standard.heading: Safe Hands-On Electronics With Instructor-Approved Equipment
mandatory_rules: 100% Low-Voltage Only: strictly powered via 3V battery packs or regulated 5V USB supplies
Zero Mains Electricity: students never connect to or handle 230V household AC power
Zero Soldering: all connections use breadboards, alligator clips, or solderless jumper wires
Manufacturer-Approved Battery Packs: non-rechargeable alkaline cells with correct polarity; no unapproved lithium packs
Safe Power Protocols: power is always disconnected before re-routing breadboard wires
Current Limiting Protection: all external LEDs use current-limiting resistors; motors are never connected directly to signal pins
Instructor Safety Pre-Check: all circuits must be inspected and approved before power is applied

microbit_v2_technical_accuracy.primary_hardware: BBC micro:bit V2/V2.2 (Nordic nRF52833 / Interface Processor Revision)
key_features: 5x5 Red LED Matrix (25 individually addressable LEDs with light-level estimation)
Two programmable physical tactile buttons (Button A and Button B)
Capacitive touch sensor logo on the front panel
On-board MEMS microphone with LED indicator and built-in speaker for audio alerts
Combined 3-axis accelerometer and magnetometer (compass) for motion and orientation detection
On-chip temperature estimation (die temperature used for environmental thresholds)
25-pin edge connector (3 large rings for alligator clips: 0, 1, 2, 3V, GND; 20 small pins)

portfolio.title: Robotics & Physical Computing Inventor Portfolio
portfolio.description: Three distinct, student-built physical computing prototypes demonstrating mastery of microcontroller programming, sensor thresholding, circuit assembly, and engineering troubleshooting.

deliverables.title: Sensor-Based Alert Device
deliverables.description: A functional micro:bit prototype that continuously reads environmental or movement sensor data (shake/tilt, light level, or temperature), applies threshold conditions, and triggers an LED animation or audible alert.
deliverables.evidence: Design brief, MakeCode program file, sensor threshold documentation, test table with normal/edge readings, and recorded bug-and-fix log.

deliverables.title: Interactive Input/Output Device
deliverables.description: A physically interactive project (such as a digital choice selector, reaction timer, or button-controlled LED alert system) connecting external physical switches or buttons with breadboard-mounted LEDs and sound output.
deliverables.evidence: Input/output system diagram, breadboard wiring plan, MakeCode code file, physical hardware test results, and student explanation.

deliverables.title: Original micro:bit Invention
deliverables.description: An independently designed and assembled physical computing invention addressing a real-world problem (e.g. desk movement alarm, study timer, plant light monitor, or low-voltage servo indicator). Includes complete engineering documentation and a live parent showcase.
deliverables.evidence: Design brief, system block diagram, parts list, MakeCode program, test record with failure analysis, documented prototype improvement, and private parent showcase presentation.

assessment_model.title: Physical Computing & Engineering Design Assessment Rubric

breakdown.description: Understanding the Input-Process-Output model, microcontrollers, low-voltage limits, and strict circuit safety rules
Proficiency in event-driven programming, variables, loops, conditionals, and synchronizing code with hardware responses
Accurate sensor calibration, selecting appropriate threshold values, noise awareness, and data interpretation
Clean solderless breadboard wiring, correct component polarity, isolating wiring faults vs software bugs, and safe iteration
Solving an authentic problem, complete engineering documentation, meaningful prototype improvement, and clear verbal explanation

criteria: Strict compliance with low-voltage electrical safety: no short circuits, correct LED polarity, and power-off rewiring
Working MakeCode program running on physical micro:bit hardware (not just in the simulator)
Methodical troubleshooting: isolating whether an error is a code bug, a loose wire, or a sensor threshold issue
Honest test documentation recording both passes and initial failures with reasoned fixes
Confident live student demonstration explaining how the invention works and what was improved
unacceptable_criteria: Connecting DC motors or heavy inductive loads directly to micro:bit signal pins without an approved driver
Attempting any high-voltage mains AC or hazardous unapproved battery connections
Submitting purely simulated projects without validating physical hardware operation
Presenting teacher-built circuits or copied tutorial projects without understanding or ability to explain them
Submitting three identical button/LED scripts with minor text changes

**Safe Low-Voltage Hardware Prototype & Wiring Documentation**
Do not connect DC motors directly to micro:bit signal pins.
Servos can create current demands beyond what the micro:bit board can safely provide.
Use the officially recommended suitable power and control configuration for the chosen servo.
Do not connect the positive terminal of an external servo/motor power supply to a micro:bit signal or power input unless the specific approved design and electrical documentation explicitly permit it.
Any separate motor supply arrangement must be reviewed by a qualified instructor and wired according to manufacturer guidance.
